summary: Registered named UI resource entry: a three-word intrusive-list anchor, a pack handle for the loaded resource, the resource-type descriptor it was loaded as, an inline 64-character name, and a handle registered with the UI table manager.
evidence: Ui_NamedEntry_InitFromName (0x004BB77C) self-links words 0/4/8, stores &maybe_g_resourceTypeDescriptor at +0x10, memcpy's min(strlen+1,0x3f) bytes into +0x14, loads the resource with Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple(...,5,&self->f_14,descriptor) and registers it with func_003882F0; Ui_NamedEntry_Dtor (0x004BBAC0) releases the handles at +0xC and +0x13C and frees.

fields.name: maybe_listNext
fields.evidence: Ctor writes *(int *)self = self, *(int *)(self+4) = self and *(int *)(self+8) = self: the entry starts with a three-word circular intrusive-list anchor (next pointer at +0). Only +0 is a separate batch offset; +4/+8 are the matching prev/self words.

fields.name: packHandle
fields.evidence: Ctor: self->f_c = self->f_c & 0xFFFFF000 | 0xFFFFF000 then Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign(&self->f_c, ...); Dtor releases it with Pack_ReleaseHandle. 4-byte pack handle.

fields.name: resourceType
fields.evidence: Ctor stores &maybe_g_resourceTypeDescriptor here and passes it as the last argument of Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple(...,5,&self->f_14,descriptor).

fields.name: name
fields.evidence: Ctor clamps the copy length to 0x3f and memcpy's the name into self+0x14, then stores the 16 stacked words as +0x14..+0x53; the Dtor frees/nulls the cached name buffer. NUL-terminated inline string.

fields.name: unknown_18
fields.evidence: Word 4 of the inline 64-byte name buffer that starts at +0x14 (char name[0x40]); listed separately only because the batch records each 4-byte memcpy store.

fields.name: unknown_1C
fields.evidence: Word 5 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_20
fields.evidence: Word 6 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_24
fields.evidence: Word 7 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_28
fields.evidence: Word 8 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_2C
fields.evidence: Word 9 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_30
fields.evidence: Word 10 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_34
fields.evidence: Word 11 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_38
fields.evidence: Word 12 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_3C
fields.evidence: Word 13 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_40
fields.evidence: Word 14 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_44
fields.evidence: Word 15 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_48
fields.evidence: Word 16 of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_4C
fields.evidence: Last word (chars 56..59) of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: unknown_50
fields.evidence: Final word (chars 60..63) of the inline 64-byte name buffer at +0x14 (memcpy store of the ctor).

fields.name: maybe_registeredHandle
fields.evidence: Dtor calls Pack_ReleaseHandle(self+0x4f), i.e. byte +0x13C (0x4f*4), and releases a second handle just before it; the ctor registers the resource with the UI table manager, so this is most likely that registration handle. Last word of the 0x140-byte record.

summary: Name-entry window with a kana keyboard: three 0x50-byte Ui_AnimRef label pages at +0x4C, the kana grid multi-list, an active-page flag at +0x148 and the hiragana/katakana keyboard pages at +0x14C/+0x19C.
evidence: Ui_NameEntry_BuildKanaGrid (0x0021DD7C) dispatches vtable +0x38 per grid cell, binds 'keyboard_hiragana' at +0x14C and 'keyboard_katakana' at +0x19C through Ui_AnimRef_Bind, reads byte +0x148 and resets both pages; Ui_NameEntry_Dtor (0x0021E19C) destroys two 0x50-byte objects at +0x14C and three at +0x4C with stride 0x50 via std_destroy_range, then calls Ui_Object_DtorBase, so the object spans 0x4C..0x1EB and derives from Ui_Object.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_NameEntry_Dtor stores 0x0075C154/0x0075A184 in *win and Ui_NameEntry_Ctor stores its vtable argument; every virtual dispatch goes through it.

fields.name: animContext
fields.evidence: BuildKanaGrid: ldr r5,[r4,#4] then Ui_AnimRef_Bind(&page, r5, "keyboard_hiragana"/"keyboard_katakana", 0) - the owner/context the page bindings resolve their panes through.

fields.name: labelAnims
fields.evidence: Dtor: std_destroy_range(self+0x13 (=0x4C), 0x003E04BC, 0x50, 3) - three consecutive 0x50-byte Ui_AnimRef label pages; BuildKanaGrid builds their labels from the 'null_txt_0' template.

fields.name: unknown_D0
fields.evidence: Only the ctor at 0x0021DD64 mentions a Container_MultiList_ClearAll at a +0x34-relative address. A 0x108-byte Container_MultiList cannot start at +0xD0 because that region is already the second/third 0x50-byte label page, so the exact kana-grid base is unresolved.

fields.name: unknown_E0
fields.evidence: Apparent field is really vtable slot +0x38 (0x38*4): the evidence line (**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x38)) is a virtual call, not a member access.

fields.name: unknown_120
fields.evidence: Apparent field is really vtable slot +0x48 (0x48*4) used for the keyboard page switch; not a data member.

fields.name: isKanaPageActive
fields.evidence: BuildKanaGrid: ldrb r0,[r4,#0x148]; when non-zero both keyboard pages are reset (Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes) and strb r5,[r4,#0x148] clears it.

fields.name: hiraganaPage
fields.evidence: Ui_AnimRef_Bind(self+0x14C, ctx, "keyboard_hiragana", 0); Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(self+0x14C, 0.0f) when the page flag is set. Dtor destroys it as a 0x50-byte object.

fields.name: katakanaPage
fields.evidence: Ui_AnimRef_Bind(self+0x19C, ctx, "keyboard_katakana", 0); destroyed by the same std_destroy_range(0x50,2) as the hiragana page.

summary: Group of UI 'entry' helpers dominated by Ui_Entry_GetDisplayText (entry-id -> display string); the only member-level evidence is a style-descriptor alpha byte, so this class is weakly defined.
evidence: Ui_Entry_GetDisplayText (0x00646728) takes (table, entryId), bounds entryId by 0x1B6 and resolves item/skill/monster display strings from the data manager; the other functions grouped here are a style-descriptor filler (maybe_Ui_Entry_FillStyleParam 0x004A56D0, writes style+0xE=0xFF) and two field-NPC talk-attribute getters (0x00641DAC/0x00641CE0) that do not touch this object at all.

fields.name: maybe_styleAlpha
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_Entry_FillStyleParam writes *(u8 *)(style + 0xE) = 0xFF (an opaque alpha) on the style descriptor passed in; that descriptor is not proven to be this class.

fields.name: unknown_620
fields.evidence: Only evidence is *(float *)(*param_1 + 0x188), a double indirection: 0x188*4 = 0x620. Not a field of self.

summary: List entry that owns an optional 0x40-byte child block: the setter releases the previous block through Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries and re-initialises the new one with Save_SlotTable_Init.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ListEntry_SetChild (0x002E6B14) guards on self->f_c and self->f_5c, releases the old child via Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries(self), allocates and zeroes a 0x40-byte block (Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x40,...)), stores it at self+0x5C and calls Save_SlotTable_Init(child, self->f_c, arg3, arg2). Its only caller is Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateSlots.

fields.name: maybe_parentSlotTable
fields.evidence: Guarded non-null and passed as the second argument of Save_SlotTable_Init(child, self->f_c, arg3, arg2), so it is the slot table the child block is built from.

fields.name: childBlock
fields.evidence: Holds the 0x40-byte block allocated by Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x40, *(u32 *)(self+8), 4); checked non-null and released through Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntries when replaced.

summary: Monster-book list entry: vtable at +0 and a 16-bit slot value at +0x94; the recovered ctor is truncated and the monster-book page itself belongs to a larger 0x11xx object.
evidence: maybe_Ui_MonsterBookEntry_Ctor (0x00244768) stores vtable 0x0075C904 in *self and zeroes the 16-bit field at +0x94 of the 0x98-byte embedded object it allocates; Ghidra loses control flow after 0x002447B8 (unaff_r9/unaff_r10, halt_baddata), so only the header is trustworthy.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_MonsterBookEntry_Ctor stores the class vtable 0x0075C904 in *self.

fields.name: unknown_94
fields.evidence: Only zero-initialised by the ctor (puVar3->f_25 = 0 with a u32* base = byte +0x94); no reader found.

summary: One 0x24-byte completion record of the progress/achievement table: a validity byte and a 0..110 percentage, recomputed from the matching 0x30-byte source entry.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ProgressEntry_RecalcPercent (0x00313BCC) finds the record among eight 0x30-byte source entries at self+0x130, scales (current-baseline)/(max-baseline)*10+100 (or current*100/target) into 0..110, then stores 1 at self+i*0x24+0x2AC and the percentage at self+i*0x24+0x2B0.

fields.name: maybe_recordValid
fields.evidence: RecalcPercent writes 1 here after recomputing the matching record; the address advances by 0x24 per record index.

fields.name: percent
fields.evidence: Stores the computed 0..110 value (func_0011CD80 ratio + 100); the +0x2AC/+0x2B0 pair repeats every 0x24 bytes.

summary: Scene-entry pool table owned by the game work (work+8 -> f_4C): two identical pools of 36 0x2C-byte position entries, each pool preceded by a 0x480-byte header; Add/AddWithOffset append a position and AllocSlot takes the first free slot.
evidence: Disassembly of Ui_SceneEntry_Add (0x00622534): entry = self + i*0x2C, transform at entry+0x480, flags at entry+0x484/+0x485; AddWithOffset (0x006224F8) first reserves in the pool at self+0x54 and then scans the pool at self+0xB10. Each pool therefore spans 0x480 + 36*0x2C = 0xAB0 bytes, so the object ends at 0xB10+0xAB0 = 0x15C0. The pointer is (work+8)->f_4C, the scene/2D position manager used by Ui_Message_CreateSceneNode.

fields.name: maybe_sceneEntryPoolA
fields.evidence: Pool base passed to Ui_SceneEntry_Add/AllocFirstFreeSlot; its 36 slots of 0x2C bytes start 0x480 bytes into the pool (vector at +0x480, flag=0 and byte1=0xFF mark a free slot).

fields.name: maybe_sceneEntryPoolB
fields.evidence: Second pool with the same layout; Ui_SceneEntry_AddWithOffset inserts into both 0x54 and 0xB10, and the 36 slots from +0xB10+0x480 end exactly at 0x15C0.

summary: Character-entry widget (party-member name/status row) deriving from Ui_Object; its class methods print the member name at +0xCA and broadcast to the widget's 'txt' panes.
evidence: Ui_CharacterEntry_Ctor (0x004ADD04) calls Ui_Object_CtorBase then stores vtable 0x00776164; the scalar deleting dtor at 0x004ADD1C is vtable slot +4 of that table. Sibling methods on the same vtable print the party-member name (func_0035EB98 member+0xCA) and broadcast to the 'txt' panes.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_CharacterEntry_Ctor stores 0x00776164 in *self after the Ui_Object base ctor; the dtor is slot +4 of it.

summary: Popup/balloon value-row list: up to 96 12-byte rows (each with an object pointer at row+8) and a row count at +0x480; the many Spawn* helpers grouped here post popup entries to the battle UI.
evidence: Ui_PopupEntry_HasDifferingValues (0x00645BAC) iterates self->f_480 rows at self+i*0xC and dispatches vtable +0xD4 on the pointer at row+8; Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList (0x003FC9F0) reads the same count, averages the row shorts and allocates a 0x21C-byte popup packet, copying the count into packet+0x214.

fields.name: rowCount
fields.evidence: Loops `i < self->f_480` over 12-byte rows (pointer at row+8) and is copied into the popup packet at +0x214; 0x480 bytes / 0xC = 96 rows.

summary: Panel node of a window resource: owner link at +0x14, state bytes at +0x1C/+0x1D, a shared UI base vtable at +0x578 and two intrusive list link pairs at +0x580/+0x58C.
evidence: Ui_PanelNode_Init (0x0019CD0C) clears byte +5, sets +0x1C=0x13, calls the owner at +0x14 (vtable +0x14, arg 1) and zeroes +0x1D/+0x20/+0x24; maybe_Ui_PanelNode_Dtor (0x0019CCAC) stores 0x00759388 at +0x578, unlinks the link pairs at +0x580/+0x584 and +0x58C/+0x590, then frees. Caller is Ui_WindowResource_ResetAndInit.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Dtor stores its vtable argument in *self (class vtable), the standard polymorphic-panel head.

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: Init reads self->f_14 and dispatches (**(code **)(*self->f_14 + 0x14))(self->f_14, 1), so it is the owner object owning the pane slot.

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: Init sets self->f_1c = 0x13 (initial panel state id).

fields.name: maybe_stateFlag
fields.evidence: Init writes 0 here (self->f_1d = 0); adjacent to the state byte, purpose not proven.

fields.name: unknown_20
fields.evidence: Only zero-initialised by Ui_PanelNode_Init (self->f_20 = 0); no reader found.

fields.name: unknown_24
fields.evidence: Only zero-initialised by Ui_PanelNode_Init (self->f_24 = 0); no reader found.

fields.name: baseVtable
fields.evidence: Dtor stores the shared UI base vtable 0x00759388 at +0x578 (a second vptr for the embedded base sub-object).

fields.name: maybe_link0Next
fields.evidence: Dtor unlinks the embedded list node at +0x580/+0x584: iVar1=*(+0x580), iVar2=*(+0x584), then iVar2->prev=iVar1 and iVar1->next=iVar2 (next pointer).

fields.name: maybe_link0Prev
fields.evidence: Prev pointer of the same intrusive list node at +0x580 (see link0Next).

fields.name: maybe_link1Next
fields.evidence: Dtor unlinks a second list node at +0x58C/+0x590 with the same next/prev pattern (next pointer).

fields.name: maybe_link1Prev
fields.evidence: Prev pointer of the second intrusive list node at +0x58C (see link1Next).

summary: Scene/hierarchy node: parent pointer at +0x18 (refcounted SetParent), the manager link at +0x04 and the layout-object pair at +0x30/+0x34 used by the shared named-pane text setter.
evidence: Ui_Node_SetParent (0x001BC750) walks the candidate parent's +0x18 chain to reject cycles, increments the parent refcount at parent+4 and stores the new parent at node+0x18; Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText (0x001A619C) only looks a pane up when both +0x30 and +0x34 are non-zero; Ui_Node_FindBaseChild (0x001B8688) resolves the manager through node+4.

fields.name: parent
fields.evidence: Ui_Node_SetParent: cycle walk `iVar2 = iVar2->f_18` up this link, refcount++ on the new parent, refcount--/vtable+8 on the old one, then *(node+0x18) = parent.

fields.name: maybe_layoutObject
fields.evidence: Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText guards on self->f_30 != 0 and uses self->f_34 as the second non-null member before Ui_Window_CollectNamedPane; +0x30 is the first layout member.

fields.name: maybe_secondaryLayout
fields.evidence: Second non-null guard before Ui_Window_CollectNamedPane; role (layout resource vs root pane) is not proven.

summary: Equipment-window scene node: a child node pointer at +0x4C whose vtable +0x14 is called with state 2, and an 'Open_Back' UI transition animation.
evidence: Ui_EquipmentWindowNode_TriggerState2 (0x0040897C) reads self->f_4c and dispatches (**(code **)(*child + 0x14))(child, 2) after func_00669DD4 accepts the trigger; Ui_EquipmentWindowNode_PlayOpenBackAnimation (0x004089B8) calls vtable +0x84 with "Open_Back" and arms a 60-frame timer; the deleting dtor (0x00408A60) calls base 0x005F8528 and frees.

fields.name: childNode
fields.evidence: TriggerState2: self->f_4c is non-null-checked and its vtable slot +0x14 is invoked with state mode 2.

fields.name: unknown_210
fields.evidence: Evidence is vtable slot +0x84 (0x84*4 = 0x210): (**(code **)(*self + 0x84))(self, "Open_Back") is a virtual call, not a data member.

summary: Per-character glyph slot passed to the UI node builder; the only recovered function resolves the font/glyph record for a char code and forwards the slot pointer into a node-create parameter block.
evidence: Ui_GlyphNode_CreateFromCharCode (0x004EDF38) takes UiGlyphSlot* self, resolves the font manager and glyph records via 0x0063E05C/0x0063FDAC/0x002D6AF8, copies up to 0x1f text characters and calls func_0035FF3C(app->f_60,f_5c,0,&params) to create the node; self itself is only stored into the parameter block, never dereferenced.

fields.name: unknown_04
fields.evidence: The quoted access pfVar6[1] * local_f4 indexes maybe_g_defaultBasisVector2 (a global), not this object; no member access to self+4 was found.

fields.name: unknown_08
fields.evidence: The quoted access pfVar6[2] * local_f4 indexes maybe_g_defaultBasisVector2 (a global), not this object; no member access to self+8 was found.

summary: Animation node: a 4-byte anim reference at +0x4C that is set through Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame during node teardown/refresh.
evidence: maybe_Ui_AnimNode_Release (0x00289EA0) passes &self->f_4c to func_00649BD4 (a two-instruction tail that adds 8 and jumps) and then to Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame; the same pair is used on the same node type at 0x0028A244. Only the 0x50-byte tail is referenced, so the node layout is otherwise unknown.

fields.name: maybe_animHandle
fields.evidence: Address of this 4-byte tail word is passed to Ui_AnimRef_SetFrame and to func_00649BD4, which forwards to the same setter; a small anim handle/reference at the end of an 0x50-byte node.

summary: Dual-line message buffer: mode byte, two 0x200-byte text line buffers at +0x2 and +0x202, then a cursor/attribute block at +0x404..+0x420. struct_db scaled this batch's offsets by 4 because it typed self as a u32 pointer.
evidence: Ui_MessageBuffer_Init (0x0061555C) takes u8* self: *self = mode; func_001113EC clears 0x200 bytes at self+2 and at self+0x202; then zeroes +0x404, copies the global at 0x007AC424 into +0x408, zeroes +0x40C/+0x410/+0x414/+0x418, sets +0x41A = 0xFFFF, +0x41C = 0 and +0x420 = 0. The batch lists these accesses at 0x808/0x1010/... which are exactly 4x the byte offsets.

fields.name: mode
fields.evidence: Ui_MessageBuffer_Init (0x0061555C) writes *self = mode before clearing the two 0x200-byte line buffers; this offset is not scaled (self is a u8 pointer at this access).

fields.name: secondLineBuffer
fields.evidence: True byte offset 0x202: func_001113EC(param_1+0x202, 0x200) clears the second 512-byte text line buffer; the batch's 0x808 = 0x202*4.

fields.name: unknown_1010
fields.evidence: True offset +0x404, only zeroed by the initialiser; purpose unknown (batch offset 0x404*4).

fields.name: maybe_defaultAttribute
fields.evidence: True offset +0x408: initialised from the global word at 0x007AC424, a default text attribute/colour value (batch offset 0x408*4).

fields.name: unknown_1030
fields.evidence: True offset +0x40C, only zeroed by the initialiser; purpose unknown.

fields.name: unknown_1040
fields.evidence: True offset +0x410, only zeroed by the initialiser; purpose unknown.

fields.name: unknown_1050
fields.evidence: True offset +0x414, only zeroed by the initialiser; purpose unknown.

fields.name: unknown_1060
fields.evidence: True offset +0x418, a byte field cleared by the initialiser; no reader found.

fields.name: maybe_noEntryIndex
fields.evidence: True offset +0x41A: set to 0xFFFF by the initialiser, a 'no entry' sentinel value.

fields.name: unknown_1070
fields.evidence: True offset +0x41C, only zeroed by the initialiser; purpose unknown.

fields.name: unknown_1080
fields.evidence: True offset +0x420, a byte field cleared by the initialiser; no reader found.
